title: Sweet Taste of Liberty
cn: 第 3 集 · 自由的滋味
novel:
Barney had a theory: [[liberty|liberty]] tastes best when the plan is [[spontaneous|spontaneous]].

So he dragged Ted to the airport at nine at night. They had no bags, no hotel, and no [[itinerary|itinerary]] — only two cheap [[boarding passes|boarding pass]] to Philadelphia. Ted said it was [[reckless|reckless]]. Barney said the word he liked was "[[thrill|thrill]]".

They [[sprinted|sprint]] through the [[terminal|terminal]] with [[adrenaline|adrenaline]] burning in their legs, [[wandered|wander]] past the wrong [[gate|gate]] twice, and were nearly stopped by [[security|security]] because Barney kept smiling like a criminal.

On the plane he told two [[strangers|stranger]] that they were rich brothers. It was [[ridiculous|ridiculous]]. It worked.

In Philadelphia the night was warm and the city was [[restless|restless]]. Ted felt young again. He was [[tempted|tempt]] to phone Robin and say something brave.

Then a guard [[detained|detain]] Barney for climbing on a famous bell, and for one long hour Ted [[regretted|regret]] everything.

There were no [[handcuffs|handcuffs]] in the end, and nobody had to pay [[bail|bail]]. At dawn the two of them sat on the airport floor, laughing, tired, and strangely proud.

"Freedom," Barney said, "is just a mistake you [[escape|escape]] from before breakfast."

liberty.en: the right to do what you want, without control from others

itinerary.en: a plan of a trip: where you go and when

boarding pass.en: the paper or card you must show to get on a plane

reckless.en: doing dangerous things without thinking about the risk

sprint.en: to run very fast for a short distance

terminal.en: the building at an airport where people get on and off planes

adrenaline.en: the chemical your body makes when you are excited or afraid

wander.en: to walk slowly with no clear direction

gate.en: the door at an airport where you get on your plane

security.en: the people and checks that keep a place safe

ridiculous.en: very silly; making people laugh at you

restless.en: unable to stay still or calm

tempt.en: to make someone want to do something

detain.en: to keep someone in a place, usually by the police

regret.en: to feel sorry about something you did

handcuffs.en: metal rings that police lock on a person's wrists

bail.en: money paid so that a person can leave prison before the trial

escape.en: to get away from a place or a danger
